style: Say casually and naturally, like a friendly teenager explaining something
lines: Drag the eye height slider and watch the horizon stay with your eyes.
Now try Turn. The red dots are your two vanishing points. An arrow at the edge points to one off the page.
Turn on Guides under Overlays to see where every edge runs.
Every edge runs to one of the two dots. That's two-point perspective.
Every edge runs to one of the three dots. The up-and-down edges meet at the third. That's three-point perspective.
Drag a building to move it, or add one from Buildings. Then press Ink to draw over your city.
Now compose. Make the tallest tower feel huge: a low eye, a wide lens, the horizon low. Then press Ink.
Your city is empty. Tap Tower, Block, Slab, Stepped or Water tower under Buildings to add one.
Windows show on faces big enough to hold them. Try a longer lens or a lower eye.
One vanishing point just went off the page. The lines still aim at it.
Tilting makes the up-and-down edges meet too. That's a third vanishing point.
Your ink was drawn for the old camera. Press Keep it, or Clear it.
Drag to draw. Your lines snap to the vanishing points.
Drag on the drawing to make a line. It snaps to a vanishing point, an upright or a level line. Hold Shift for a free line.
Drag on the drawing to make a line. Snap is off, so aim each line at its vanishing point yourself.
Drag over a face of a building to hatch it. The lines aim at that face's vanishing point.
Pick Light, Mid, Dark or Dusk, then tap a face to fill it.
Drag across a line, a hatch or a fill to erase it.
Keep drawing, or try Hatch and Fill. Then press Check my drawing to test lines drawn by eye.
Snap is off now. Draw building edges by eye. Any line that misses its vanishing point turns red.
Fix the red lines. Erase one, then draw it again toward its vanishing point.
Every line hits its point now. Write what you changed, then press Done.
Set the eye height, turn and lens to match the outline, then press Check camera.
When you think your camera matches, press Check camera. It tells you which setting to read next.
This outline looks up, so use Tilt too.
Press Next target for a new outline.
That was the last one. Press Start over to go back to target 1, level again.
Read the eye height: the outline's horizon crosses every building at the camera's eye height, and more roof means a higher eye. Press Extend outline edges.
Read the turn: press Extend outline edges, then turn until your red dots sit under the outline's amber ones.
Read the lens: the farther apart the outline's vanishing points, the longer the lens. Close together means a wide lens.
Read the tilt: the outline's up-and-down edges lean together. Tilt until yours lean the same.
Your city is off the page. Move Horizon on page, or pick a wider lens.
Matched.
